claim_summary: For the printed SL8I amplitude-controlled flow \(\dot x=my-y^2,\ \dot y=az^2+xy,\ \dot z=bx^2+cxy\) with \(a,b,c,m>0\), every compactly supported invariant Borel probability measure \(\mu\) satisfies the exact stationary identities \(\langle y^2\rangle=m\langle y\rangle\), \(\langle xy\rangle=-a\langle z^2\rangle\), and \(\langle x^2\rangle=(ac/b)\langle z^2\rangle\). Hence \(0\le\langle y\rangle\le m\), \(\langle y^2\rangle\le m^2\), \(\langle z^2\rangle\le cm^2/(ab)\), and \(\langle x^2\rangle\le c^2m^2/b^2\). These bounds are sharp: \(\langle y\rangle=0\) occurs only for the origin point mass; \(\langle y\rangle=m\) (equivalently \(\langle y^2\rangle=m^2\)) occurs exactly for measures supported on the three equilibria with \(y=m\); and either outer \(x\)- or \(z\)-second-moment bound is attained exactly by measures supported on the two nonzero equilibria \(E_\pm=(-cm/b,m,\pm m\sqrt{c/(ab)})\). Therefore every non-equilibrium ergodic compact recurrent state, in particular every nonconstant periodic orbit, satisfies all three outer amplitude bounds strictly. At the article's parameters \(a=1/2,b=3/5,c=6/5\), the identities reduce to \(\langle x^2\rangle=\langle z^2\rangle\), \(\langle xy\rangle=-\langle z^2\rangle/2\), and \(\langle y^2\rangle=m\langle y\rangle\), with the sharp RMS envelope \(\operatorname{RMS}(y)<m\) and \(\operatorname{RMS}(x)=\operatorname{RMS}(z)<2m\) for every non-equilibrium ergodic compact recurrent state.
integrity: All algebraic identities and equality cases were reconstructed from the printed vector field; no numerical trajectory evidence is used as proof.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is conditional on compact support of the invariant measure and does not prove global boundedness.
It does not establish existence, uniqueness, physicality, or ergodicity of the numerically displayed chaotic attractor.
The theorem is stated for system (5) exactly as printed and does not rely on any normalization equivalence with earlier displayed forms.
title: Sharp stationary moment envelope for the amplitude-controlled SL8I flow
